confirmed.sharpenedFix: The seat diagnosis is right, one of its four repairs does not work, and it missed the worst case. THE WORSE CASE: after Tab the focus is on the carried card OWN TICK, and onKey returns early for .tick, so pressing Space there marks the task done and moves it to the done lane WHILE aria-grabbed=true and data-force=moving are still set - a card simultaneously in hand and completed. Ctrl+Z then unwinds only the completion (back in the in progress column) and leaves both the original todo->doing move unrecoverable AND the grabbed state still on. THE BROKEN REPAIR: the seat focusout guard tests whether relatedTarget is inside .card[data-id=carriedId]; I measured that Tab moves focus INTO that same card (its tick), so the guard never fires on exit (b) - the exact exit the seat names. Two changes make it work: test focus leaving the CARD ELEMENT ITSELF, not its subtree (its own controls are not part of the hand), and do not hang it on focusout at all - every arrow press calls mount(), which tears the card out of the DOM and fires focusout with a null relatedTarget, so a focusout guard would cancel the carry on the first arrow. Intercept Tab in onKey instead - if (key === "Tab" && carriedId) commitCarry() before the native tab proceeds - which is deterministic and has no mount-timing race. Keep the seat other three repairs, all of which I verified are needed: lift the Space commit block into commitCarry(); call it from endCarry() so the pointer exit arms too; call endCarry() before openCard() in the Enter branch. For the product switch, the site is go() at src/app.js:447 and endCarry is module-local to tasks.js, so it needs an entry on the existing registry.tasks.api surface (alongside rows/add/remove/reveal) rather than a direct call. Finally, note what already works and must not regress: Tab then Escape still cancels correctly, and Tab then Shift+Tab then Space still commits with a receipt and a live undo.
